subject: Archaeology
title: Roman Roads: Paths That Shaped Europe
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Roman Roads: Paths That Shaped Europe.

hook.text: Roman roads were so well built that many are still followed by modern highways today.

buildup.text: Engineers layered gravel, sand, and stone slabs with drainage ditches on each side.

discovery.text: Over 250,000 miles of roads connected the empire. The network took centuries to build.

twist.text: Roads were military tools first. Legions needed to march fast. Trade came second.

climax.text: LiDAR and aerial photos keep revealing lost Roman roads under modern fields.

punchline.text: Roman engineers built roads to last forever. They nearly succeeded.

quiz.question: What was the primary purpose of Roman roads?
options: Military movement so legions could march quickly across the empire
Connecting religious temples and sacred sites across provinces
